image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a sea lion resting on a rocky surface. The animal is lying on its side with its head tucked down and eyes closed. A large foreflipper is prominently displayed in the foreground, draped over the rock. The fur appears short, coarse, and brownish-tan. The background consists of out-of-focus grey rocks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad with prominent sagittal crest in males.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible but angled downwards and partially obscured by the resting posture. While the head appears broad, the specific anatomical feature of a 'prominent sagittal crest' cannot be clearly verified due to the angle and lack of profile view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: External ear pinnae (visible ear flaps) distinguish from true seals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A distinct, small external ear flap (pinna) is clearly visible on the side of the head, just behind the eye area. This confirms it is an eared seal (Otariid) and not a true seal.
Long, light-colored whiskers are clearly visible extending from the muzzle area against the darker fur of the face.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Fur is short and coarse ranging from brown to dark grey, lighter on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible fur texture is short and appears coarse. The color is a uniform brownish-tan. The ventral surface is not clearly visible to confirm the 'lighter' gradient, but the dorsal coloration matches.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits streamlined fusiform form of substantial marine mammal proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the torso shows a thick, robust, and tapered shape consistent with a fusiform marine mammal body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Males develop thick neck mane and are significantly larger than females.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: It is impossible to determine sex or compare size to females from this single image. No distinct thick neck mane is clearly visible due to the resting posture and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Foreflippers are large, broad, and hairless on underside used for terrestrial locomotion.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The large foreflipper is the focal point of the lower center. It is broad and appears to have sparse hair or bare skin on the visible surface, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Hind flippers can rotate forward for walking on land.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The hind flippers are completely occluded by the body and the rock; they are not visible in the frame.
The animal is lying on its side in a curled/resting position. Bilateral symmetry cannot be assessed from this asymmetrical pose.

The transition from the head to the neck/body appears somewhat smoothed out. The anatomical definition of the neck muscles is lacking, making the head look slightly fused to the torso rather than connected by a distinct neck structure.
